subject: Draft DPA: scope for non-adaptive processing, subprocessors, and transit assurances
messages:
From: Sara Mason <sara.mason@truwellhealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@truwellhealth.com
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft DPA: AI usage & non-adaptation clause — initial asks

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the quick intro yesterday. I've attached our initial DPA draft (TruWell-DPA-draft-v1.docx) and call out three items that are blocking procurement/legal sign-off on the pilot:

1) No-adaptive processing / "no-training" commitment — we need explicit clause that TruWell data will not be used to update or fine-tune any models, private or shared, and a description of the operational proof we can request at onboarding.

2) Prompt/response ownership and derivatives — the draft currently says Redwood keeps "derivative rights". We need clarity that customer prompts and generated responses are owned by TruWell and that no derived model artifacts based on our data will be transferred or used.

3) Subprocessors & cross-border transit — please provide an up-to-date subprocessors list, and confirm the flow for onshore processing in the EU (SCCs were mentioned in your doc, but we need specifics on whether data can transit outside the EU and what controls are in place).

Operational asks:
- Evidence pack for no-train: what does Redwood provide? Log samples? KV/ephemeral caching proof?
- If we need an escrow or escrow-like escrow for derivatives, what's Redwood's recommended path?

Attached: TruWell-DPA-draft-v1.docx (redlined).

We're hoping to get a proposal we can show procurement by next week. Can you loop in whoever handles security/ops proof?

Thanks,
Sara Mason
Head of Legal Operations
TruWell Health

--

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sara Mason <sara.mason@truwellhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 09:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft DPA: AI usage & non-adaptation clause — initial asks

Hi Sara — thanks for the detailed redline and the clear asks. Quick responses below and we've attached the subprocessors snapshot for today (redwood-subprocessors-20261007.pdf).

High-level options for the pilot (we can scope details into SOW/DPA):
- Option A (strict): No-adaptive processing — Redwood will agree to a contractual prohibition on using TruWell inputs/responses for model training or fine-tuning. Processing is stateless/ephemeral for the pilot (no persistent KV caching of prompt-response pairs beyond the ephemeral request lifecycle). We will provide an operational evidence pack (see items below).

- Option B (scoped telemetry): Allow minimal telemetry (aggregate, de-identified telemetry for runtime improvements) but not for model parameter updates. This is an engineering tradeoff — we can document the exact telemetry and retention.

Prompt/response ownership: we can accept language that acknowledges TruWell retains ownership of input prompts and generated outputs for the customer's account. We will include an explicit carve-out that Redwood retains right to feature-flag, bugfix and service-quality telemetry, but not to re-use prompts/responses for model training or to create derivative models.

Subprocessors and transit: attached list includes primary cloud provider endpoints and our managed inference partners. For EU onshore routing we can commit to pinned region processing (no egress outside EU region) for the pilot, subject to capacity & pricing. We can also add SCCs for cross-border when needed.

Operational proof (what we'll provide):
- Subprocessor inventory & contact points (attached).
- A one-time "no-train evidence pack": example audit logs showing no model update calls, sample request/response retention settings, and a runnable ops checklist.
- Optional: KMS configuration snapshot or confirmation (onshore KMS available for EU customers with an addendum).

Escrow/derivatives: Redwood's recommendation is an escrow of model snapshots is heavyweight; instead we propose contractual restrictions + periodic ops attestations and a retention/export path for customer-owned copies of generated data. If TruWell insists on formal escrow, we can scope costs.

I've looped in David (privacy/legal) to propose precise DPA language and the evidence template. Marissa will coordinate pricing impact for pinned EU routing.

Next steps: David will send suggested clause text, and Marissa will provide a cost/throughput estimate for onshore-only processing. If that looks good, let's schedule a 30-minute working session next week with procurement.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Privacy & Ops
Redwood Inference

--

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Sara Mason <sara.mason@truwellhealth.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 10:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft DPA: AI usage & non-adaptation clause — initial asks

Hi Sara / Grace — thanks. I've drafted two short clause options and an evidence checklist attached (no_train_clause_suggestion.txt). High-level notes:

1) Clause wording (two variants):
- Variant 1 (strict no-train): "Redwood shall not use, reproduce, or incorporate Customer Data, including prompts and generated outputs, to train, fine-tune, or otherwise adapt any model (public or private) now or in the future. Redwood will implement operational controls to prevent such use and will provide an evidence pack on request."

- Variant 2 (operationally bounded): same as above, but allows for "service-quality telemetry" that is aggregated and non-identifiable; explicit list of telemetry types must be included as an exhibit.

2) Evidence pack (what we can deliver for onboarding or audit):
- Snapshot of subprocessors and region routing for the account.
- Audit log excerpts showing lack of model-training API calls from the account.
- Storage retention config for request/response: confirmation that storage retention is set to ephemeral (TTL) for the pilot.
- KMS binding evidence (if customer selects onshore KMS).
- Operator attestation signed by Redwood SOC/OPS lead (PDF).

3) Prompt/response ownership: Proposed DPA excerpt: "Customer retains ownership of Customer Data and Generated Outputs. Redwood shall have no rights to use Customer Data to create derivative models unless explicitly agreed in writing." That should address procurement's IP ask.

4) Cross-border / SCCs: We can add SCCs as an exhibit; for EU-only pinning we will reserve capacity and scope any pricing delta. Note: EU pinning is operationally feasible for pilot, but we need the expected QPS and peak concurrency to size capacity — Marissa, can you provide an estimate for TruWell?

If TruWell wants an escrow model snapshot or third-party audit, we'll need to price that separately — standard legal approach is to avoid escrow unless required by regulator.

I've attached the clause file and the evidence template. Happy to revise wording to match your redlines in TruWell-DPA-draft-v1.docx.

Thanks,
David Kim
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Mason <sara.mason@truwellhealth.com>

Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft DPA: AI usage & non-adaptation clause — initial asks

David / Grace — this is helpful, thanks. TruWell is comfortable with Variant 1 (strict no-train) + the operational evidence pack you outlined, provided the following are added to the DPA:

- Explicit statement that "Customer retains exclusive ownership of prompts and generated outputs."
- A 30-day SLA for delivery of the one-time evidence pack after the pilot kick-off (we'll accept a documented attestation if the full log extracts are sensitive).
- Confirmation that pinned EU routing will be in place for the pilot and that any capacity constraints or pricing deltas will be communicated before the pilot start.

Procurement asks me to confirm budget; deal id TW-2026-1098. Can Marissa scope the EU-pin pricing delta and expected throughput guidance?

If we can get a clean DPA + evidence timeline by end of next week, procurement will greenlight the pilot. Also happy to do the 30-minute call — can do Wed or Thu next week morning CET.

Best,
Sara Mason
Head of Legal Operations
TruWell Health
